Text: The two forms release the same medicine at different speeds, and they are approved for different conditions. Metoprolol tartrate is released all at once, so it acts sooner and wears off sooner. Metoprolol succinate is released slowly over the day, so one dose lasts about 24 hours. Only the extended-release form is approved for heart failure and for children, and only the immediate-release form is approved for use after a heart attack.
Metoprolol tartrate | Metoprolol succinate
Release | Immediate release | Extended release
Usual dosing | Once or twice a day, or every 6 hours after a heart attack | Once a day
Forms | Tablet, injection | Tablet, capsule
Tablet strengths | 25 mg, 37.5 mg, 50 mg, 75 mg, 100 mg | 25 mg, 50 mg, 100 mg, 200 mg
Brand names | Lopressor | Toprol-XL, Kapspargo Sprinkle
Approved for heart failure | No | Yes
Approved after a heart attack | Yes | No
Approved for children 6 years and older | No | Yes
Triplet: ["Metoprolol", "approved for", "heart failure"]

The relation 'approved for' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject form of the drug is approved for use in treating the medical condition specified by the object entity.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. B. 'has dosage form': The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
C. 'used in population': The subject drug is used in or approved for the patient population or age group specified by the object entity.
